subject: Planned runtime stewardship: staged driver refresh & customer coordination (APAC1)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Planned runtime stewardship: staged driver refresh & customer coordination (APAC1)

Hi Priya —

Quick note to let you know we have a planned, narrowly scoped driver/hotpatch cycle for APAC1 next week. Summary below — full runbook attached. We wanted to surface details early and offer an explicit opt-in/opt-out for customers who have very tight change controls.

What: staged host driver update + short node-level restarts. This is a post-release hotpatch to address a detected scheduling inefficiency and a low-severity driver memory leak.
When: Tuesday, 22 Jul 2025, 02:00–06:00 UTC (regional rollout across APAC1). We will sequence hosts to keep per-tenant disruption minimal.
Scope & expected impact:
- Affected surface: shared-host inference pools in APAC1 (host-level restarts, ~3–8 minutes per host); dedicated/reserved pools are not scheduled for drains in this run (we will NOT evict dedicated allocations without explicit customer approval).
- Typical customer effect: brief tail latency increases for a small percentage of requests during host handover; if a request is in-flight and affected, the runtime will transparently retry to a compatible host. No model weights will be reuploaded.
- Mitigation: automatic prefix/KV cache warmup and short-lived fallbacks to our lower-latency model variant for critical routes.

Action for FinApps:
- If you are comfortable with the standard rolling approach, no action is needed.
- If you require exclusion or a maintenance freeze for a specific pool, please click the opt-out link below by 20 Jul 2025 23:59 UTC. We will honor requests for dedicated pools and for named routes where change windows are restricted.

Links & attachments: runbook and impact matrix attached. Opt-in/opt-out: https://redwood.app/opt-in-form?id=FIN-8472

I'll loop Ops and CS in the thread for any last-mile clarifications.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_apac_hotpatch_runbook_v2.pdf (PDF)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finapps.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 10:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned runtime stewardship: staged driver refresh & customer coordination (APAC1)

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the heads up. A couple quick questions for our SRE and procurement teams:
1) Will our dedicated inference pool (finapps-dedicated-apac1) be touched? We rely on pinned capacity for latency SLAs.
2) If we experience an interruption that breaches our SLA, is there a standardized credit process (we have an active commit)?
3) Are encryption keys or KMS rotations part of this maintenance? We have tight key rotation controls.

We may opt-out if dedicated capacity is at risk; otherwise we prefer to be excluded only for named routes and sensitive customer workloads.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Reliability, FinApps, Inc.
priya.shah@finapps.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 11:24:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned runtime stewardship: staged driver refresh & customer coordination (APAC1)

Hi Priya —

Thanks — answering inline below and looping Sean (Ops) and Marissa (CS) for specifics and to document any opt-outs.

1) Dedicated pools: confirmed — we will NOT evict or drain reservations for finapps-dedicated-apac1 as part of this change. The driver patch is being applied to shared-host pools and read-only control-plane agents; dedicated capacity remains untouched unless you explicitly request us to schedule a reservation migration.

2) SLA credits: our standard incident postmortem/credits policy applies if a customer experiences measurable downtime outside normal SLO. Given the nature of this operation (short host handovers with automatic retries), we do not anticipate SLA-qualifying outages. That said, if FinApps records a measurable impact, we'll start a credits review. Marissa — can you please flag this for the billing/CS playbook in case FinApps files a ticket?

3) KMS/keys: no KMS rotations or key material changes are part of this work. Keys remain unchanged; access/rotation schedules are separate and will not be affected.

Additional notes: we've added an impact matrix that maps endpoints -> probable latency delta. For FinApps, the routes to watch are: /v1/generate (text-gen-v1) and /v1/chat (chat-pro). Both have fallback routing configured to lower-cost variants for brief handovers.

If you'd like us to mark any specific route or API key as "maintenance-excluded," reply with the route names and we'll register the exclusion. Opt-out deadline: 20 Jul 2025 23:59 UTC.

Sean, can you confirm the expected cadence (hosts/hour) and a point-contact for any on-call escalations?

Best,
Grace

Attachment: impact_matrix_apac1.csv (CSV)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finapps.com>

Grace —

Appreciate the prompt, and thanks for confirming the dedicated pool status and KMS details. We reviewed with our SREs and we'll accept the standard rolling approach for shared pools. Please exclude these routes from any changes: /v1/payment-verify and /v1/customer-secrets (they're sensitive flows proxied via the API key finapps-prod-01). We'll keep our opt-out request limited to those two routes.

Also please provide the on-call escalation number for the maintenance window (we'll add it to our runbook).

Thanks —
Priya
